title: Records with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Personnel recalled: Arnett Nelson, Harmon Edwards, Burton, Lee Collins, and New York sessions.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: He was learning, you know, kids he was learning, but he was doing fine. A lot of those kids are smart, very smart. You just have to take pains with them though.
Well, I was going to ask about those records you made for Jelly Roll Morton, and we played the Tiger Rag and Weary Blues. Can you tell anything about that session, who all was on that?

That's what I want to say. I know some of those fellas, but some of those guys got away from me. There were some of them that left Chicago. I don't know where they went to, but I know they left here, but I do know that Arnett Nelson was with us, because many times Arnett Nelson used to tease Jelly Roll, you know. Jelly Roll had a place down in the loop, you know. And he used to be down there, he wore derby, you know, in long shoes. Them guys draw the picture of Jelly Roll and made him mad. You know Jelly Roll, don't you? I know, yes. Yeah, yeah, yeah. He got mad, guys got sober with him, but he come all right after, he's all right. But this guy, Arnett, myself, and Jelly Roll had two or three fellas there, I didn't know from over on the north side. He lived way over on the, way over on Sedgwick, over there, Harmon Edwards. He lived over on Sedgwick and the fella played bass fiddle. Bass fiddle, what is his name? That's a Burton too. He played with the other role. Burton, I don't know what's his first name. Burton, bass tuba player. He quit playing. Lee Collins. Yeah, and Lee Collins was with us. And let's see who else. Did Lee use the cornet then or trumpet, I guess? Lee played the trumpet. I believe he had a half from a medium side, you might call it a cornet and a medium side.
He played. Remember anything about that, whether those records were made, they were right here in Chicago, wasn't it? Yeah, all the records were made, they were right here in Chicago.

And most of all, outside the door we made in New York with Fatten and the banjo player, we made them, we went to New York and made them. But it wasn't with Jethro then, we made them, not with some of the numbers, we made in New York with Melrose, see? Melrose. Let's see, yeah, Melrose, we made most of, a lot of those numbers with Melrose. I wish I could get a good number and put on the records, you know, to show them trombone and play it hard to play. Yeah, I wish you could too. Yeah. I'm going to get together and practice. I'd like to hear you. I've never heard you in person except for the records. Well sir.
Yeah, I know. Well you'd be just as happy as you would if you were sitting and listening that. I'd do a bit more, you know, just.
Yeah, I know. I can tell from those records, I've heard everybody talk so much about how wonderful you were. Yeah.
I used to get a lot of praise.
